title: Energy taxation directive
subtitle: Revision requiring unanimity — not adopted
voteRuleLabel: Unanimity — one member state can stop it
summary: The revision of minimum energy tax rates failed again. Twenty-three member states were in favour, two against and two abstained — and on a tax file, unanimity means the two against are enough. The minimum rates in force date from 2003.
whatItMeans: Nothing changes: the 2003 minimum rates stay in force.
Tax files need every member state, so an abstention does not block but a single no does.
The debate now moves to whether energy taxation should leave unanimity behind.

outcome.headline: Not adopted — two member states against, and unanimity is required.
